question:
**Select the correct option:**

Neither the principal investigator ________ the co-authors anticipated the backlash.
solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. nor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses a correlative conjunction pair "**neither**" and "**nor**" to indicate that both the principal investigator and the co-authors did not anticipate the backlash.
 
• Option "**nor**" is grammatically correct because it complements "**neither**" in this structure.
 
• Other options, such as "or", "and", or "nor did", do not fit the grammatical structure of this sentence.

Correct sentence: *Neither the principal investigator **nor** the co-authors anticipated the backlash.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neither...nor:**

 
 
• This pair of correlative conjunctions is used to join two negative ideas.
 
• **Example:** Neither the team members nor the coach were prepared for the match.
 
• **Usage:** Ensures both parts of the sentence are negative.
 
 
 
• **Other conjunctions:**
 
 
• "Or" is used to present alternative options, but does not fit in this sentence.
 
• "And" is used to connect two positive or neutral ideas, which is not appropriate here.
 
• "Nor did" introduces a new clause and is not suitable for this sentence structure.
